articles.title: Satin Chrome
articles.summary: Full-metal chrome body with a broad soft satin highlight instead of a mirror; brushed-metal luxury. Reads as your existing colours turned into soft, brushed-looking chrome; the highlights are broad and gentle instead of mirror sharp, so the car looks like satin stainless or pewter.
articles.what: Satin chrome (250/45/40) — chrome-tier metal with a broader, softer highlight. Up close: Dead smooth: the paint and all three spec panels are one uniform tone with no grain, brush marks, flake or pattern. It is a pure spec change (metal 250, roughness 45, clearcoat 39) that leaves your paint pixels as they are. From a distance: Reads as your existing colours turned into soft, brushed-looking chrome; the highlights are broad and gentle instead of mirror sharp, so the car looks like satin stainless or pewter. Measured spec (average): metal 250, roughness 45, coat 39. Shine: high gloss. Metal: full. It takes the colour you give the zone.
when: Best on: body, trim, hero panel.
Fits: gt / sports car, show car, open wheel.
how: Click the zone you want to change.
Click the BASE MATERIAL box (it says "Click to choose a base") and type "Satin Chrome" in the SEARCH FINISHES box.
Click it to open the big preview, then click Apply.
Pick your colour with BASE COLOR.
Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: Whole body: a spec-only treatment suits any size panel
Hero panels like hood and roof show the soft highlight best
Numbers keep their colour and stay fully legible; just avoid very dark numbers on very dark paint since the metal can wash them.
Bold livery stripes and shapes: colours stay sharp over the soft metal
Pairs well with: black, satin, pearl, red.
pitfalls: Not mirror chrome: roughness 45 spreads highlights, there are no sharp reflections
Not matte or flat paint: metal is 250, it glows and reflects broadly
Avoid: next to mirror chrome, big dark areas in the sim.
articles.spec_character: Average spec: metal 250 (chrome or mirror tier), roughness 45 (high gloss), clearcoat 39 (strong-to-medium clearcoat). The spec is almost perfectly flat, one smooth material.
articles.intent_note: Spec-driven shelf: the shine does all the visual work and your own paint colour stays as it is.
articles.paint_advice: Reflection inherits the paint colour: near-white paint gives silver, a coloured paint gives tinted chrome, and a dark paint stays dark. Avoid: next to mirror chrome, big dark areas in the sim.

combos.why: Patterns that suit it: bold livery stripes and shapes: colours stay sharp over the soft metal; fine linework and outlines: no texture to fight them
Patterns to avoid: fine glitter or flake: pointless noise on a smooth satin base
Spec overlays that work: fine brushed streak spec: makes it a true brushed-metal look; light ripple or wave roughness: adds a soft liquid shimmer
Judge the paint and the shine together: the same spec looks different under different colours.

articles.title: Flat Black

Looks like your own paint with all shine killed: dead flat, chalky, with no reflections; with black it becomes the murdered-out flat black look, with any other colour a dull flat version.
articles.what: Dead flat, zero coat (0/250/255) — the darkest response the paint side of the cube has. Up close: A perfectly flat, textureless surface: the paint is untouched and every shine map is one uniform value (metal 0, roughness 249, clearcoat 250). No grain, flake or pattern at any zoom; it only removes all gloss from your colour. From a distance: Looks like your own paint with all shine killed: dead flat, chalky, with no reflections; with black it becomes the murdered-out flat black look, with any other colour a dull flat version. Measured spec (average): metal 0, roughness 250, coat 255. Shine: matte. Metal: none. It takes the colour you give the zone.

how: Click the zone you want to change.

Click it to open the big preview, then click Apply.
Pick your colour with BASE COLOR.
Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: Whole body: the flat look only works when it is even across panels

Pairs well with: gloss, chrome, red, white.

Spec overlays that work: gloss clear stripe spec: glossy bands on dead flat, a ghost-stripe look; fine sparkle spec: tiny glints to break up the dullness

Click the BASE MATERIAL box (it says "Click to choose a base") and type "Semi-Gloss" in the SEARCH FINISHES box.
Click it to open the big preview, then click Apply.
Pick your colour with BASE COLOR.
Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: Whole body: uniform sheen suits all panels
Hood and roof for a broad soft highlight
Numbers read cleanly in any colour; the even sheen adds no texture.
Any graphics, stripes or camo: a pure spec base is a clean canvas for them
Pairs well with: black, white, red, chrome.
pitfalls: Not full gloss: highlight is wider and softer
Not satin or matte: reflections still read
Avoid: high-gloss finishes, heavy textures.
articles.spec_character: Average spec: metal 0 (non-metal paint), roughness 60 (satin gloss), clearcoat 16 (maximum clearcoat). The spec is almost perfectly flat, one smooth material.
articles.intent_note: Spec-driven shelf: the shine does all the visual work and your own paint colour stays as it is.
articles.paint_advice: Gloss shows the paint colour as it is, so any colour works; pick the colour for contrast with the neighbouring zones, not for the finish. Avoid: high-gloss finishes, heavy textures.

combos.why: Patterns that suit it: any graphics, stripes or camo: a pure spec base is a clean canvas for them; fades and gradients: even gloss shows colour changes cleanly
Patterns to avoid: chrome or mirror patterns: base is not reflective enough
Spec overlays that work: fine micro-texture spec: breaks the flat gloss for a more real look; gloss/matte stripe spec: contrast bands without recolouring
Judge the paint and the shine together: the same spec looks different under different colours.

articles.title: Sentient Polycarbonate
articles.summary: Warm maroon-orange ember surface with fine gold sparkle and soft molten glow, high gloss. Reads as a warm, glowing ember red-orange with a fine glitter shimmer; the cloud mottling gives it a molten depth.
articles.what: Clear optical polymer with internal color shift — changes tone under different lighting angles Up close: Mottled red-orange ember: dark maroon cloudy patches with lighter orange-peach clouds 20-40 px, and a field of tiny bright orange-red four-point sparks (about 4 px) scattered evenly across it. From a distance: Reads as a warm, glowing ember red-orange with a fine glitter shimmer; the cloud mottling gives it a molten depth. Measured spec (average): metal 184, roughness 33, coat 16. Shine: high gloss. Metal: high. It brings its own colours.
when: Best on: body, hood, hero panel.
Fits: gt / sports car, show car, stock car.
how: Click the zone you want to change.
Click the BASE MATERIAL box (it says "Click to choose a base") and type "Sentient Polycarbonate" in the SEARCH FINISHES box.
Click it to open the big preview, then click Apply.
Leave BASE COLOR on Use finish's own color to keep its colours.
Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: Whole body: the warm mottle works on every panel
Hood and roof: show the sun glints best
White or black numbers with a thick outline read well; mid-orange tones disappear into the field.
None or a clean stripe: the ember field is already full
Pairs well with: black, chrome, gold, dark grey.
pitfalls: Not candy paint: the colour is cloudy with bright sparks, not a smooth transparent red
Not a chameleon: the render shows no colour travel, only red-orange
Avoid: dark graphics may lose contrast under strong highlights, next to other high-sparkle finishes.
articles.spec_character: Average spec: metal 184 (true metallic), roughness 33 (high gloss), clearcoat 16 (maximum clearcoat).
articles.intent_note: Spec-driven shelf: the shine does all the visual work and your own paint colour stays as it is.
articles.paint_advice: It brings its own colours, so leave BASE COLOR on the finish's own colour. Put it next to a plain zone of the opposite sheen (matte beside gloss, warm beside cool) so the colours have a calm neighbour. Avoid: dark graphics may lose contrast under strong highlights, next to other high-sparkle finishes.

combos.why: Patterns that suit it: none or a clean stripe: the ember field is already full; fine pinstripes in gold or black: add trim without clutter
Patterns to avoid: flake, glitter or other iridescent patterns: stack sparkle on sparkle; busy camo or weave: muddy the ember clouds
Spec overlays that work: gloss clearcoat sheet: already high gloss, deepens the depth; none: spec is already smooth and shiny
Judge the paint and the shine together: the same spec looks different under different colours.

articles.title: Wet Look
articles.summary: Mirror-smooth high-gloss lacquer with a razor-tight highlight, no flake or texture. Reads as your own colour under a deep, razor-clear lacquer: crisp mirror-like highlights on curves, otherwise perfectly plain.
articles.what: Razor-wet lacquer — the tightest highlight a dielectric paint can have (0/15/16). Fresh-detailed concours depth. Up close: Completely flat in paint and in all three spec panels: metal 0, roughness 15, clearcoat 16, no flake or grain. It takes your colour; the grey is only the placeholder. From a distance: Reads as your own colour under a deep, razor-clear lacquer: crisp mirror-like highlights on curves, otherwise perfectly plain. Measured spec (average): metal 0, roughness 15, coat 16. Shine: high gloss. Metal: none. It takes the colour you give the zone.
when: Fits: show car, gt / sports car, stock car.
how: Click the zone you want to change.
Click the BASE MATERIAL box (it says "Click to choose a base") and type "Wet Look" in the SEARCH FINISHES box.
Click it to open the big preview, then click Apply.
Pick your colour with BASE COLOR.
Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: Whole body: neutral and safe everywhere
Hood, roof and fenders: curves show the tight highlights best
Numbers keep their colour; strong reflections on curves can cut contrast on dark numbers in bright sun.
Any stripe, graphic or camo: the clear lacquer makes them look dipped and deep
Pairs well with: any colour, chrome, black, white.
pitfalls: Not Soft Gloss: roughness 15 vs about 30, so the highlight is tighter and wetter
Not chrome: metal is zero, you still see your colour
Avoid: strong reflected highlights can reduce contrast on dark graphics, authored wear is optional, not part of the material.
articles.spec_character: Average spec: metal 0 (non-metal paint), roughness 15 (wet mirror gloss), clearcoat 16 (maximum clearcoat). The spec is almost perfectly flat, one smooth material.
articles.intent_note: Spec-driven shelf: the shine does all the visual work and your own paint colour stays as it is.
articles.paint_advice: Gloss shows the paint colour as it is, so any colour works; pick the colour for contrast with the neighbouring zones, not for the finish. Avoid: strong reflected highlights can reduce contrast on dark graphics, authored wear is optional, not part of the material.

combos.why: Patterns that suit it: any stripe, graphic or camo: the clear lacquer makes them look dipped and deep; fine metal flake or glitter overlay: wet depth over sparkle gives a show-car look
Patterns to avoid: none; neutral base
Spec overlays that work: gloss/matte stripe bands: dull stripes against razor-wet paint; fine sparkle spec: adds shimmer without colour change
Judge the paint and the shine together: the same spec looks different under different colours.
